key_insight: A simulation-trained deep learning platform can automate and standardize interpretation of CDC and FCXM HLA antibody assays, reducing operator dependence in pre-transplant compatibility testing.
clinical_relevance: By improving the consistency and traceability of physical crossmatch readouts, the tool may support more reliable donor-recipient matching before transplantation.
method: Trained a UNet-based model on simulated CDC-like microscopy images spanning wide technical variability.
Combined automated lymphocyte segmentation, experiment-specific fluorescence classification, and well-level cytotoxicity scoring.
Added automated FCXM support with cell population identification and IgG readout interpretation through a web-based interface and API.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, automated CDC scoring performed within the range of human inter-annotator variability and outperformed a rule-based pipeline under variable acquisition conditions.
watch_item: Performance is shown in simulated and retrospective diagnostic workflows, so real-world deployment will still need external validation across sites, instruments, and assay protocols.
paper_title: Simulation-Trained Deep Learning for Automated Cell-Based HLA Antibody Assay Interpretation in Pre-Transplant Diagnostics
